text_version.note: AGORA record covers part of an act: State of Arizona Senate Bill 1565, An Act Amending Sections 16-442, 16-552 and 16-621, Arizona Revised Statutes; Relatin

territorial_scope.description: Applies to voting systems and elections for federal, state and county offices in Arizona.

evidence.quote: Machines, devices, firmware or software used in this state may not include any artificial intelligence or learning hardware, firmware or software.

summary.short: Would amend Arizona election statutes to bar artificial intelligence or learning hardware, firmware and software from voting machines and devices used in federal, state and county elections, from early ballot processing, and from electronic vote adjudication. No effective date appears in the text; registry metadata lists the bill as failed.
summary.long: Senate Bill 1565 would amend three Arizona Revised Statutes provisions on election administration. Section 1 amends A.R.S. 16-442: machines, devices, firmware or software used in the state may not include artificial intelligence or learning components; the secretary of state must adopt standards for loss of certification after consulting a committee; the secretary of state may revoke certification or prohibit for up to five years the purchase, lease or use of a voting system in connection with federal, state or county elections; and emergency certification of an upgrade is limited to six months. Section 2 amends A.R.S. 16-552: artificial intelligence or learning software or firmware may not be used in processing early ballots or by the early election board in verifying the voter's affidavit. Section 3 amends A.R.S. 16-621: any electronic vote adjudication feature may not include artificial intelligence or learning software or firmware; the county officer must provide live video recording of ballot custody in tabulation rooms for statewide, county and legislative elections, contingent on legislative appropriation; and chain-of-custody records must be kept from early voting through provisional tabulation. The text states no effective date. Registry metadata records the bill as failed.](string-placeholder)}]}</br>{

notes: Registry metadata gives status failed (legislative_stage dead). The document has no enactment clause, effective date or legislative history. Amended sections appear as plain text without strike-through or underline, so new material cannot be separated from restated text in this copy; capitalised 'ARTIFICIAL' (Sec. 2 A) and 'INTELLIGENCE' (Sec. 2 B) may mark inserted words. The three amended sections are coded in one row for the Arizona Revised Statutes. Sec. 2 B contains the wording 'software of firmware' where 'software or firmware' seems intended.
